oneOf.comment: http MCP server written into each agent's config.

agents.comment: Optional: only configure this server into these agents (default: all).

enabled.comment: Optional: set false to add the server flagged disabled, toggleable in the agent UI (default true; Claude has no disable flag so it is omitted there).

provisionCommands.comment: Custom bash commands run, in array order, on EVERY provision -- AFTER this profile's repos are cloned and the SDKs installed. The working directory is this profile's first repo checkout (WORKSPACE_ROOT/<dir>), or WORKSPACE_ROOT when the profile declares no repo. All repository checkouts finish before this stage starts. Independent profiles run in parallel; commands inside each profile stay ordered. Later stages wait for all profiles. PROVISION_JOBS=1 restores sequential profile order; scripts using shared resources must coordinate or run sequentially. Run as root. Install all project requirements on a fresh VM; on reprovision reuse satisfied installations and caches, install or repair missing/outdated requirements, and update only when the project intentionally tracks newer versions. Respect pins and lockfiles. Prefer incremental commands such as npm install over clean reinstalls such as npm ci; preserve user configuration and report real failures. A failing command is logged but does not abort provisioning or the remaining commands.

forwards.comment: Ports to expose with `construct expose`, requested on EVERY provision after the provisioning commands (get-or-create: a reprovision never opens a second forward for the same port and target). Forwards are VM state that a reinstall deletes; listing one here is what brings it back. `to` defaults to client (a tunnel to the user's PC); host asks the host service for a LAN port. `https: true` asks for an HTTPS forward with the host's certificate (docs/https-forwards.md), a host forward that must say what its port speaks: `upstreamTls` false for plain HTTP, true for TLS (`construct expose --upstream-plain` / `--upstream-tls`); the host never guesses. `name` is `--name`. Where the host offers no HTTPS for the VM it opens a plain host forward instead. Removing an entry does not close a live forward.
